title: Integrate Liquity V1 Stability Pool for LUSD Collateral Yield
body:
## Problem
Plain LUSD collateral earns 0% yield. Integrate Stability Pool for ~6.28% APR ([Dune data](https://dune.com/liquity/liquity-v1)) to fund governance token buybacks, without disrupting liquidity.

## Solution
Add `StabilityPoolFacet` via diamond proxy. Auto-deposit LUSD to pool on mint; withdraw principal on redeem. Harvest ETH/LQTY yields during redeems for buybacks/compounding (protocol-owned only). Piggyback ops on user txs for gas efficiency.

## Alternatives Considered
- AAVE (~3.24% yield, more complex).
- Leverage/LPs (higher risk).
- V2 migration (future option for multi-collateral).

## Implementation Spec
### ~~Prerequisites~~
- ~~Audit facet (~$10-20K budget).~~
- ~~Integrate `IStabilityPool.sol` (address: 0x66017D22b0f8556afDd19e1e5b5f1cbD89a6C337).~~
- ~~Add 1inch/Uniswap for swaps.~~
- ~~New storage: `totalPrincipalInPool` (uint256), `protocolTreasury` (address).~~

### Facet Functions
- `depositToPool(uint256 amount)`: Call `provideToSP(amount, address(0))`.
- `withdrawFromPool(uint256 amount)`: Call `withdrawFromSP(amount)`.
- `harvestRewards()`: Claim rewards, swap (e.g., 50% to LUSD for compounding, 50% to governance token for buybacks).

### Flows
- **Mint**: Transfer LUSD → Deposit to pool → Mint uUSD → Update `totalPrincipalInPool += amount`.
- **Redeem**: Burn uUSD → Calc principal → Withdraw/transfer principal → Harvest if rewards > threshold (route to treasury) → Update `totalPrincipalInPool -= amount`.

### Over-Collateralization
Value pool as LUSD equivalent (Chainlink oracles for ETH/LQTY). Redemptions: principal only.

### Monitoring/Automation
- Chainlink/Gelato for optional harvests. It would be nice to sell the ETH/LQTY for LUSD and boost holdings as soon as it is rewarded by the stability pool.
- Dune alerts for APR/supply.

## Testing
- Unit: Deposit/withdraw/harvest (Foundry).
- Integration: Mainnet fork; simulate liquidations.
- Edges: Low liquidity, volatility, mass redeems. Gas: <200K extra per tx.

## Deployment
1. Deploy facet.
2. `diamondCut` via multisig.
3. Verify on Etherscan.
4. Phased: Opt-in for new deposits.

## ~~Risks/Mitigations~~
- ~~Yield variability: Fallback to plain LUSD if APR <3%.~~
- ~~Supply crunch: Auto-withdraw if < $10M.~~
- ~~Security: Audit for reentrancy.~~

title: Staking v2 audit
body:
Depends on https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/985

We must audit the newly created staking contracts.

Scope:
1. https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/StakingFacet.sol
2. https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibStaking.sol

Staking use case example for an end user:
1. User [stakes](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/StakingFacet.sol#L64) `LUSD/UUSD LP` tokens from [Curve pool](https://etherscan.io/address/0xcc68509f9ca0e1ed119eac7c468ec1b1c42f384f) 
2. Some time passes
3. User [unstakes](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/StakingFacet.sol#L69) position and collects [UBQ](https://etherscan.io/address/0x4e38D89362f7e5db0096CE44ebD021c3962aA9a0) rewards

Notes:
- Staking code is based on [MasterChef](https://github.com/sushi-labs/sushiswap/blob/271458b558afa6fdfd3e46b8eef5ee6618b60f9d/contracts/MasterChef.sol)
- Auditor should consider how the staking feature works in context of the diamond pattern and [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) where users are able to:
  a) send [LUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0x5f98805a4e8be255a32880fdec7f6728c6568ba0) and [UBQ](https://etherscan.io/address/0x4e38D89362f7e5db0096CE44ebD021c3962aA9a0) in order to mint [UUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0xb6919Ef2ee4aFC163BC954C5678e2BB570c2D103)
  b) redeem [UUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0xb6919Ef2ee4aFC163BC954C5678e2BB570c2D103) in order to get [LUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0x5f98805a4e8be255a32880fdec7f6728c6568ba0) and [UBQ](https://etherscan.io/address/0x4e38D89362f7e5db0096CE44ebD021c3962aA9a0)

I suppose staked token must never be the same one used as collateral in [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) because it may skew calculations [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L354) and [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L717).

title: CI: fix `check_storage_layout` for new contracts
body:
There's the [core-contracts-storage-check](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/20799bedf5ee4d40d2863653f7bc2fe68a2ce3fa/.github/workflows/core-contracts-storage-check.yml) workflow which checks that contracts' storage is not messed on contract upgrades.

Check these CI runs which fails with the `No workflow run found with an artifact named...` error:
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/actions/runs/11125075713/job/30912062971?pr=959
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/actions/runs/11145695030/job/30975996318?pr=971

The issue is that when a **new contract** is added the [core-contracts-storage-check](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/20799bedf5ee4d40d2863653f7bc2fe68a2ce3fa/.github/workflows/core-contracts-storage-check.yml) starts to fail while the expected behavior for the CI workflow to pass because we don't need to check storage layout for newly added contracts (because storage of the newly added contract hasn't been updated hence storage collision could not occur).

So as a part of this issue we should make sure that:
1. [core-contracts-storage-check](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/20799bedf5ee4d40d2863653f7bc2fe68a2ce3fa/.github/workflows/core-contracts-storage-check.yml) is not failing for newly added contracts
2. [diamond-storage-check.yml](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/20799bedf5ee4d40d2863653f7bc2fe68a2ce3fa/.github/workflows/diamond-storage-check.yml) is not failing for newly added libraries

P.S. Pls provide a QA in the related PR with these scenarios:
1) No storage updates, CI passing
2) Storage update, no collision, CI passing
3) Storage update, collision, CI failing
4) New contract added, CI passing

title: Adding collateral enabled checks for redemption collections might make users uncapable of redeming their funds.
body:
[MEDIUM] - Adding collateral enabled checks for redemption collections might make users uncapable of redeming their funds.

This PR is intended to fix [the bug described in this Sherlock issue](https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2023-12-ubiquity-judging/issues/29). However, the Sherlock report is actually wrong and the vulnerability described must not be considered as an issue in the first place, so the collateralEnabled check should not be added on collecting redemptions.

Enabling/disabling collaterals allows the protocol to add or remove supported collaterals, not to be used under uncertain situations, such as a hack. In such type of situations, the `isRedeemPaused` check can be enabled to prevent users from redeeming if something wrong is currently  happening.

The problem with adding the `collateralEnabled` check here is that if Ubiquity decides to disable a collateral in the future, some redemptions might be already queued, so users won't be able to withdraw their funds.


Recommendation: Remove the `collateralEnabled` check for collecting redemptions.

_Originally posted by @0xadrii in https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/pull/894#discussion_r1572571068_

title: Security monitoring
body:
In case of a security incident we should:
1. Pause all of the contracts
2. Notify the core team that something went wrong

Possible solutions for monitoring:
- https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-automation
- https://www.openzeppelin.com/defender
- https://cyvers.ai/

What should be done:
1. Setup monitoring for [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol). In case of a possible security incident (let's say >30% of liquidity is withdrawn) we should:
a) Pause the [UbiquityDollarToken](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/core/UbiquityDollarToken.sol)

P.S. Mainnet contract addresses can be found [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/e4c1fae5ef5e9ba40bcb84c671f2ba39f0ab5208/packages/contracts/broadcast/Deploy001_Diamond_Dollar_Governance.s.sol/1/run-latest.json)

title: Formal verification
body:
We should implement formal verification for [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol). 

So collaborator who's going to take this issue should carefully study the [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) and think of the invariants that should be tested.

Invariants could be:
- user can not mint more Dollars in USD than provided collateral
- user can not redeem more collateral in USD than provided Dollar tokens

Possible solutions for formal verification:
- https://github.com/a16z/halmos
- https://docs.runtimeverification.com/kontrol

We already had a try with formal verification, you may find related scripts [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/tree/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/scripts/smt-checker).

What should be done:
1. Impelent formal verification for the [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) contract (you may create tests in a separate test file like `UbiquityPoolFacet.formal.t.sol` so we could distinguish unit, fuzz, invariant and formal verification tests)
2. Setup testing CI to run formal verification tests on merge to the `development` branch (keep in mind that github action runnners can run for 6 hours). We don't need to run formal verification tests on eash PR since they're really time consuming.

title: Governance Token emissions to `ubq.eth` new strategy
body:
For every `1` governance token minted via our staking contract to our community members, we emit an additional `0.5` governance tokens to `ubq.eth`

I think it could be a very interesting proof of concept for future DAOs to fund development automatically by emitting governance tokens to a wallet that is controlled by the UbiquiBot for their repositories. 

What would be the simplest way to add an additional split, but within the protocol level? 

To clarify, this is a low priority task that would be used primarily for selling a future vision (this is why I think it should be implemented on the smart contract level.)

It would be great if we can set multiple emission destinations and set the amounts. That way, for example, maintenance on this repository can receive 5% of all governance token emissions, UbiquiBot repository 10% etc.

title: New Proposal Router
body:
Using vector embeddings(?) we should make a simple UI that will allow us to create any new proposal and it will automatically route it to the correct repository. 

I envision something similar to the new issue ui: https://github.com/ubiquity/.github/issues/new

But the key difference is that we will have a dropdown of where to post the issue to across all of our orgs. It will intelligently hide and show what it thinks is relevant as the user starts typing out the specification, live. 

I imagine with sufficient enough unique detail, we can turn that massive list into something as short as a few target repository options. [^01^] 

Given that we already have issue dedupe tech, I think we can achieve this pretty easily. But it isn't clear to me how to leverage that tech for this solution. This same backend will be immensely useful for the Telegram interface. You can, at any time (even in a dm) write something like: 

```
@ubiquityos we need to fix the cash out interface on pay.ubq.fi because its currently not vertically center aligned. 
```

title: Ubiquity Credit
body:
I think we have a shot at making the crypto industry's first under collateralized credit program. 

Normally you need to be over collateralized to borrow, but, we have two key points of leverage in our infrastructure that can make under collateralized credit work. 

1. Contributor reputation: we can track a contributor's earnings over time and extend credit based on their monthly average earnings. For example, a user earns on average $5000 a month for the last three months, so they can borrow $5000 from us at X% APR if they need liquidity. Not sure what a good minimum threshold is but obviously the shorter the riskier. We could start a pilot with a whitelist of OG contributors first. We can consider only allowing card minting to disincentivize the use of leverage/trading with the funds. 

2. Permits: wages are distributed through our system and could be used for automatic payback (or garnishing wages) which could help make financing easier to payback. 

I think the biggest piece of advantage is the reputation system though. Contributors who have old GitHub profiles can be more inclined to pay back debts to continue using the system if they have an old GitHub profile and worked for a long time in the system.

title: Dynamic Data Input
body:
# Dynamic Data Input on TradingView Indicator

The first major engineering challenge in order for this to be useful in realtime decision making is to allow for the script to have the capability to dynamically read position data from external data sources. I did quite a bit of research on this, and it appears that TradingView's PineScript does not currently have this capability. 

Currently the variables must be manually input on the indicator. This can be done by double clicking the indicator on TradingView.

![tv](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4975670/201572439-f6443b3e-5f1c-4abc-bc15-e8a0be86a129.jpg)

Those variables are manually imported off of the data presented by Revert's UI

https://revert.finance/#/uniswap-position/mainnet/312741

The founder of Revert passed me along this draft documentation of their private API. This was current as of 12 July 2022, as such there may have been some changes introduced since. This will allow you to access the information in JSON format. 

[apidocs.md](https://github.com/ubiquity/uniswap-v3-liquidity-provider-indicator/files/9999366/apidocs.md)

---

# Research

I would encourage you to explore workarounds.

### Workaround Strategy A - API Reverse Engineering

I would highly recommend API reverse engineering so that there is FAR LESS infrastructure to support for this capability. Then we could have a super simple node program that simply pings Revert (GET) and TradingView (POST) APIs every minute or so.

### Workaround Strategy B - Scraper

Have a remote invoked [scraper](http://github.com/ubiquity/scraper) to manually log in to your TradingView account, and

1. pass in the updated parameters using the settings panel (this might be possible by directly making the API request to update the user's settings vs having to navigate through the UI) or 
2. to hardcode the parameters and update the PineScript code.

title: Integrate Wallet Connect via Reown AppKit
body:
## Overview  
Enable seamless wallet connectivity in the dApp by integrating the Reown platform's AppKit toolkit, supporting wallet login, transaction approvals, and cross-chain interactions. This spec is focused on Ethereum-compatible chains using `WagmiAdapter`. The solution uses React/Next.js as the UI framework.

## Goals  
- Support secure wallet connections without exposing private keys  
- Provide users wallet management (login/logout, transaction signing)  
- Utilize Reown's AppKit for enhanced UX, security, and multi-chain support  

## Tools and Libraries  
- `@reown/appkit/react` - Core UI and functionality kit  
- `@reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi` - Adapter for Ethereum EVM chains  
- `wagmi` - Ethereum hooks for React wallet management  
- `@tanstack/react-query` - Data caching and syncing (used by AppKit)  

## Setup Steps

### 1. Project Initialization  
- Use Reown’s CLI to bootstrap your AppKit integration:  
```bash
npx @reown/appkit-cli
```
- Select your project name, framework (React or Next.js), and network library (`wagmi` recommended for EVM).  
- Enter project folder and install dependencies:  
```bash
cd your-project-name
npm install
```

### 2. Register Your Project on Reown Cloud  
- Create a free account at [[cloud.reown.com](https://cloud.reown.com/)](https://cloud.reown.com)  
- Create a new AppKit project; obtain the **Project ID** for configuration  

### 3. Environment Configuration  
- Create a `.env` file at the root of your repo, add:  
```env
NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID=your-reown-project-id
```

### 4. AppKit Setup in Code  
- Create a config file (e.g., `config/index.tsx`) to set up AppKit with WagmiAdapter and chains:  
```tsx
'use client';

import { createAppKit } from '@reown/appkit/react';
import { WagmiAdapter } from '@reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi';
import { mainnet, arbitrum } from '@reown/appkit/networks';

const wagmiAdapter = new WagmiAdapter({
  projectId: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID!,
  networks: [mainnet, arbitrum],
});

export const appKit = createAppKit({
  adapters: [wagmiAdapter],
  networks: [mainnet, arbitrum],
  projectId: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID!,
  metadata: {
    name: 'Your DApp Name',
    description: 'Description of your dApp',
    url: 'https://your-dapp-url.com',
    icons: ['https://your-dapp-url.com/icon.png'],
  },
  features: {
    analytics: true, // optional
  },
});
```

### 5. Wrap Your Application with AppKit Provider

```tsx

title: Display Accurate Redemption Oracle Price
body:
The user interface at `uusd.ubq.fi` is currently displaying a misleading UUSD price, which is causing confusion for users attempting to redeem their tokens. The UI shows the spot price from the Curve pool, while the smart contract uses a different calculated Time-Weighted Average Price (TWAP) to determine redemption eligibility. This discrepancy leads users to believe they can redeem when the functionality is actually blocked by the contract's security mechanisms.

## Technical Analysis

The frontend currently displays two prices:

1.  **Spot Price**: Fetched directly from the Curve pool. This is what users see as the main price.
2.  **TWAP Price**: This is the value returned by `getDollarPriceUsd` from the `UbiquityPoolFacet`, which is the actual value used by the contract for redemption checks.

The issue is that the UI does not clearly indicate that the "TWAP" price is the one that governs redemptions, and it is not prominently displayed.

## Proposed Solution

To address this, we will modify the frontend to provide users with clear and accurate information about the redemption process.

1.  **Update Price Display**:
    *   The main price displayed on the redemption page should be the value returned by `getDollarPriceUsd`.
    *   This price should be clearly labeled as "**Redemption Oracle Price (TWAP)**" to indicate its role in the redemption process and its time-averaged nature.
    *   The spot price can be retained as a secondary reference but should be clearly distinguished from the oracle price.

2.  **Add Explanatory Tooltip**:
    *   A tooltip should be added next to the "Redemption Oracle Price (TWAP)" that explains why this price is used and how it is calculated (i.e., "This is a time-weighted average price used to prevent flash loan attacks. It is calculated based on the LUSD/USD price and the UUSD/LUSD price from the Curve pool.").
    *   This will provide transparency and help users understand why redemptions may be paused.

3.  **Dynamic Redemption Message**:
    *   The UI should display a clear, dynamic message that indicates whether redemptions are currently possible based on the "Redemption Oracle Price (TWAP)."
    *   For example, if the price is above the threshold, a message like "**Redemptions are temporarily paused because the oracle price is above the $0.99 threshold**" should be displayed prominently.

## Acceptance Criteria

*   The `uusd.ubq.fi` redemption page must display the price from `getDollarPriceUsd` as the primary price for redemptions.
*   The UI must clearly label this price as "Redemption Oracle Price (TWAP)".
*   A tooltip explaining the price calculation and its purpose must be present.
*   The UI must display a clear message indicating the current status of the redemption functionality based on the TWAP.

title: Multicall3 batch contract reads
body:
Multicall3 contract allows us to make batch contract reads with one RPC call.
Instead of using Multicall3 contract on the project level, we can implement it in the rpc-manager server so it's completely invisible to the end user who is using the RPC.

Benefits:
- More efficient - less network requests
- Faster - not by a lot but theoretically it should be because there is less overhead
- Less likely to hit rate limits - this is the biggest benefit of this because a lot of public RPCs have rate limits

The proposed flow:

1. The client sends an array of RPC calls to the server
2. The server transforms those RPC calls into one RPC call to the Multicall3 contract and sends it to the upstream RPC provider
3. The server receives the response and transform all results to the original format
4. The server sends the response back to the client which can process the results normally - no modification needed on the client part

This only applies to contract reads so only if the RPC method is `eth_call` and contract writes (`eth_sendTransaction` method) is not recommended for Multicall3 because it has some caveats

title: Make text-conversation-rewards MCP Compliant
body:
To enable broader interoperability, we should make the `text-conversation-rewards` plugin MCP compliant. This would allow any LLM or external system to interact with it using the Model Context Protocol, rather than relying on UbiquityOS-specific conventions.

### Key Points & Discussion

- **MCP Integration:**  
  Use the [typescript-sdk](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk) for standard MCP integration. This may require changes to the `manifest.json` schema or an adapter for compatibility.

- **Deployment:**  
  All plugins should have a Deno Deploy endpoint. For plugins currently running as GitHub Actions, the Deno endpoint should trigger the Action (see [daemon-pricing](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pricing) for an example).

- **Streamable HTTP:**  
  MCP works through Streamable HTTP. Deno supports streaming, but it's not strictly required for all MCPs.

- **Context Handling:**  
  The main challenge is providing the necessary context (e.g., repo/issue/task info) when running outside GitHub (e.g., Telegram, CLI). Platform adapters may be needed to capture and provide this context.

- **Platform Agnosticism:**  
  `text-conversation-rewards` can be made platform-agnostic if we decouple content retrieval from GitHub and allow input from other sources (e.g., Google Docs, Telegram). The main non-agnostic part is currently content retrieval.

- **Standardization:**  
  Standardizing Deno deploy templates (similar to Cloudflare) will help. We have implemented some MCP-like standards already, but aligning with industry standards is beneficial.

- **Next Steps:**  
  - Prototype MCP compliance with `text-conversation-rewards` first.
  - Consider making a special AI system capability for plugins that use the current manifest format.
  - If successful, expand to other plugins as needed.

title: Migrate tests from Jest to Bun Test
body:
## Task: Migrate Test Suite from Jest to Bun Test

**Goal:** Replace the current Jest test runner setup with Bun's built-in test runner (`bun test`) for improved performance and simplified tooling.

**Context:**
This project currently uses Jest for running tests. Migrating to `bun test` aligns with the project's adoption of Bun for other tasks (runtime, package management) and can potentially offer faster test execution, plus should help us dealing with ESM import issues and required transformers.

**Required Changes:**

1.  **Remove Jest Dependencies:**
    *   Uninstall Jest-related packages (`jest`, `@types/jest`, `ts-jest`, `babel-jest`, `ts-node` etc.)
    *   Remove the `.babelrc` file
2.  **Remove Jest Configuration:**
    *   Delete the `jest.config.ts` file.
3.  **Update `package.json` Scripts:**
    *   Modify the test script(s) to use `bun test` instead of `jest`.
4.  **Refactor Tests:**
    *   Go through all files in the `tests/` directory.
    *   Replace Jest's global functions (`describe`, `it`, `test`, `expect`, `beforeEach`, `afterEach`, etc.) with imports from `"bun:test"`.
        ```typescript
        import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, mock } from "bun:test";
        ```
    *   Adjust test matchers as needed. While many are similar, there might be differences. Refer to the [Bun Test documentation](https://bun.sh/docs/test/writing).
    *   Update mocking logic. Replace `jest.mock`, `jest.fn`, `jest.spyOn` with Bun's mocking capabilities (e.g., `mock`, `spyOn` from `"bun:test"`).
    *   `mswjs` does not work with `bun` for network mocking. Consider looking into https://github.com/DRFR0ST/bun-bagel or mock Octokit altogether.
5.  **Verify:**
    *   Run `bun test` and ensure all tests pass successfully.
6.  **Update CI/CD:**
    *   Modify `jest-testing.yml` that execute tests to use the new `bun test` command.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

*   All Jest dependencies and configuration files are removed.
*   All tests in the `tests/` directory are successfully migrated to use `bun test` APIs.
*   `bun test` runs without errors and all tests pass.
*   CI/CD pipelines are updated to use `bun test`.

title: Reward "sub-plugins"
body:
Relates to https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel/issues/264

> Currently known as text-conversation-rewards and with its "sub-plugins" these should always return a "reward request" which implies that it will give a financial reward to the user for doing something. 

This behemoth of a plugin is scheduled for dismantling into sub-plugins to branch out the various reward features for easier development and partner integration (gives them more customizability via `premade config` options)

- [ ] `review rewards`
- [ ] `simplification incentives`
- [ ] `conversation and discussion`
- [ ] `task reward`

Each sub-plugin will use structured output to represent reward statements.

It's not clear if we'll have a single `"Rewards"` plugin which is in control of all sub-plugins or whether that'll be the kernel. By "Rewards plugin" I mean a plugin for our kernel instance that handles all of this rather than bloat up the kernel) not another partner plugin.

I suspect the kernel, which implies that the kernel will be the permit generator (or a UI, but I'm assuming the kernel for now), if each reward statement is it's own permit that's bad UX. If we are storing the reward statements somewhere and then somehow after the `"final trigger"` (whatever that may be since chains don't exist) it produces an aggregate permit. [^01^]

This has been a grey area for a long time and would need to be fleshed out first before this can be dismantled and due to the volume of suggestions this should be of high priority formalizing the rewards API.

title: Implement Differential Reward Distribution for Reopened Issues
body:
When an issue is reopened and closed again, the reward system should calculate and distribute only the difference between previously granted rewards and new rewards.

**Requirements**:
1. Track Previous Rewards
   - Store transaction history with amounts per beneficiary
   - Record payment mode (direct/permit) used for each distribution

2. Differential Calculation
   - Compare new reward amounts with previously distributed amounts
   - Calculate positive differences only (additional rewards)
   - Skip beneficiaries with no change in rewards

3. Distribution Logic
   - Only process transactions for beneficiaries with positive reward differences
   - Handle cases where original payment failed but issue was reopened

4. Error Handling
   - Validate transaction history before processing
   - Handle missing or incomplete previous distribution data
   - Log detailed comparison between old and new reward amounts

**Technical Considerations**:
- Must not conflict with wallet insolvency fallback (generates permits if wallet can't afford payouts) 
- Extend Supabase schema to track complete distribution history
- Implement comparison logic in `payment-module.ts`
- Update GitHub comment format to show differential amounts

**Example Scenario**:
```typescript
// Original distribution
{
  "user1": { total: 100, paid: true },
  "user2": { total: 50, paid: true }
}

// New calculation
{
  "user1": { total: 150, difference: 50 },
  "user2": { total: 50, difference: 0 },
  "user3": { total: 25, difference: 25 }
}
```

**Success Criteria**:
- Only processes payments for positive differences
- Provides clear audit trail of all distributions
- Handles edge cases: failed payments, partial distributions should never happen with the insolvency fallback. 
- Handle what happens if we change the mode (direct, permits only) between distributions

title: AI-Driven Task Time Estimates
body:
Relates to https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pricing/issues/82#issuecomment-2658468278

I've used AI to help keep this as short and succinct as I could, so I've left out a lot of details/ideas/direction. If any of this is approved I'll create a task list and write initial specs for each stage that was approved.


## **Structured Reporting**

To ensure both immediate usability and future scalability, this specification emphasizes the importance of structured reporting. By capturing the complete PR lifecycle—from the initial spec through discussion, coding, review, and merge—this approach provides:

- **Instant Utility:**  
  - Rapid insights via retrieval-based methods.
- **Future-Proofing:**  
  - Readily available, training-ready datasets without additional manual curation.
- **Consistency & Scalability:**  
  - A reproducible pipeline that standardizes every PR with machine-readable details.
- **Continuous Improvement:**  
  - An automatic feedback loop that enhances both the structured reports and eventual modeling outcomes.

## **Key Challenges**

The primary challenges in accurate task estimation include:

1. [^04^] **Historical Data Bias**  
   Past labels and timestamps may be misleading or applied inconsistently, which can skew estimations.

2. [^02^] **Code Context Dependency**  
   Superficially similar tasks can differ significantly in complexity due to refactoring, dependencies, or bottlenecks.

3. **Structured Data for Retrieval and Model Training**  
   While retrieval-based methods provide immediate utility, effective model training requires well-prepared historical data to avoid inheriting prior biases, which is labour intensive when done right in the context it's being suggested right now.

---

## **Proposed Approach**

The strategy involves developing structured and consistent PR lifecycle reports. These reports support both rapid, retrieval-based analysis and scalable model training by focusing on building a robust data foundation.

<details>
<summary>1. Reducing Bias in Historical Data</summary>

### **Challenge**  
Historical data often suffers from biases due to inconsistent labeling and timestamp inaccuracies.

### **Strategy**  
- **Objective PR Reviews:** Standardize reviews by treating the organization as the unit of analysis and guiding an LLM to perform objective evaluations post-merge.
- **Enhanced Data Representation:** Use codebase-aware embeddings and structured reporting to precisely track the PR lifecycle.
  
### **Implementation Steps**  
- **Data Definition & Collection:**  
  - Identify key fields such as time-to-completion, contributor roles, and lines of code changed.
  - Retrieve issue and PR data via the GitHub API.
- **PR Lifecycle Reporting:**  
  - Generate detailed, structured reports per PR that document affected areas, estimated vs. actual time, and review details.
- **Embedding & Retrieval:**  
  - Convert these reports to vector embeddings to facilitate efficient similarity searches.
- **Annotation & Validation:**  
  - Manually verify subsets of data to ensure quality.
- **Structured Output:**  
  - Export refined data in a JSONL format suitable for future model training.

</details>

---

<details>
<summary>2. [^02^] Code Context Awareness</summary>

### **Challenge**  
Surface-level similarities between tasks may conceal underlying differences in complexity derived from code changes.

### **Strategy**  
Integrate codebase-aware embeddings to assess task complexity more accurately.

### **Implementation Steps**  
- **Initial Codebase Parsing:**  
  - Implement a one-time comprehensive parsing for new partners.
- **Continuous Monitoring:**  
  - Track ongoing changes to ensure the embeddings remain up to date.

</details>

---

<details>
<summary>3. Contextual Retrieval & Model Training (w/ Full Implementation Steps)</summary>

### **Challenge**  
While effective task estimation can initially rely on retrieval-based methods, scalable improvements require refined training datasets that overcome historical biases.

### **Strategy**  
Adopt a hybrid, phased approach:
- **Immediate Stage:**  
  - Employ retrieval-based methods using structured reports to identify similar past tasks.
- **Mid-Term Stage:**  
  - Curate and normalize a dataset capturing real work metrics (e.g., actual time vs. estimated time, code changes) for training, using the structured reports.
- **Long-Term Stage:**  
  - Train and fine-tune lightweight models that compare predictions against retrieval-based baselines to progressively enhance estimation accuracy.

### **Implementation Steps**  
- **Phase 1: Retrieval-Based Estimation**  
  - Store structured PR lifecycle reports as embeddings.
  - Implement vector similarity searches to recommend comparable tasks. [^03^]
  
- **Phase 2: Data Curation for Model Training**  
  - Collect detailed historical task data using generated reports.
  - Normalize and clean the dataset to exclude anomalies, although this is unlikely to be required unless building the datasets directly from the GitHub data without post-merge AI analysis. [^01^]
  
- **Phase 3: Model Training & Iteration**  
  - Train models on the validated dataset.
  - Compare model outputs with retrieval-based estimations to adjust and improve accuracy. [^05^]
  - Incorporate a feedback loop to continuously refine predictions.

</details>

title: Incentives for lower estimates
body:
This is a draft/discussion and needs more research and ideas. 

As the DAO grows and trust naturally decreases, there should be an incentive for the author and possibly assignee for them to want to make time estimates for tasks as short as realistically possible (or just as close to accurate as possible)

Otherwise the natural incentive is to over estimate all tasks to make pricing larger than it should be. 

Currently the only soft incentive is the financier/admins/managers needing to approve a time estimate before "funding" tasks. 

#### time accuracy 

This is very tricky to do because even if it's a `<4 hour` task, in our system design it's perfectly acceptable to spread that project over a few days. Because of this, we can't simply check the timeline timestamps of when they started and when they pushed their last commit or comment to determine how long it actually took them. Finding accurate time estimates may be better suited for an LLM to be the judge but even still it might be tough to do with accuracy. RAG with all the comments in the repository may provide more clues/hints for accuracy but this still seems shaky. We could do an experiment with estimating time estimates based on RAG context and then we could consider a penalty/bonus depending on how aligned the estimate is for the LLM compared to who set the label?

It could even be revealed only when the project is closed as complete which may incentivize further the label setter to tell the truth. I.e. "accurate label set bonus reward" which can be a gradient based on how close in milliseconds the label value is to the LLM estimate.

title: Automatic Priority and Time Labeling
body:
This plugin may require vector embeddings of the issue specifications, but it seems to be a responsibility under this plugin for dealing with the labels so I'm filing here.

The system should learn from issue specifications and their labels to predict priority levels and time estimates for newly posted tasks. [^01^] 

We should be able to configure to automatically assign time, priority, and/or price labels. 

For example if 
```yml
setPriority: true
setTime: true
setReward: false
```

Then this will allow the team to approve of task pricing before allowing people to self assign. 

### Precision

This could be a second generation of this capability. It could be especially useful when computing against larger tasks in the weeks or months range.

title: Improved first time contributor DX
body:
## Enforcing Org Standards for New Contributors

It has become a regular issue that new contributors are not adhering to conventional commit standards. This leads to repetitive interactions with each pull request (PR), where we educate them about our organization-wide standards.

In other large open-source projects, bots automate initial acknowledgements of standards, such as 'accepting terms and conditions' or signing off on specific practices. I propose a similar automated approach to enforce these standards strictly.

#### High-Level Enforcement via Bot
- If CI is not green, and a `review_requested` event is triggered, the bot will apply a `requested_changes` review and comment: "CI has failed and is required before requesting a review."

#### Accommodations for First-Time Contributors
- For first-time contributors, we can utilize an API to determine if this is the contributor's first task, covering anything from `/start` to `closed_as_complete`. Or use a JSON based storage simply for `Username:HasAcknowledgedTerms`, if the user name is not present we request they accept, if it's present standard `/start` flow.
- If a contributor has not `closed_as_complete` or this is their first open PR, we should:
  - Comment on the issue (preferably) or the PR. This ensures they are aware of the guidelines upfront and do not need to backtrack and amend commits.
  - Clearly state our high-level contributing guidelines in the comment. Currently, we lack an official `contributing.md`, but we enforce several unwritten rules such as:
    - Use `yarn`
    - Ensure usage of version `v1.22`
    - Follow conventional commits
    - Always use the formatting scripts provided

#### Acknowledgement Requirement
- Implement a system where contributors must "accept" an acknowledgement of these standards before we assign the issue to them. This process:
  - Saves reviewers time by reducing the need to repeatedly educate on org-wide standards.
  - Improves Developer Experience (DX) as contributors are informed upfront, preventing the need to backtrack significantly on their PRs.
  - Enhances professionalism and presents the project as more official.
  - Helps in filtering out contributors who may find these standards too demanding or complex, ensuring a better fit for the project's needs.

### Benefits
- **Time Efficiency:** Streamlines the review process by setting clear expectations from the start.
- **Improved DX:** Reduces the burden on new contributors by providing clear guidelines upfront.
- **Professional Image:** Enhances the project's professionalism and operational efficiency.
- **Quality Control:** Helps maintain a high standard of contributions by ensuring all contributors adhere to set practices.

### This plugin or a new one?

A dedicated plugin would be great actually as we could allow for a lot more customization of the terms and standards etc by allowing them to pass in their own custom markdown for tables etc as opposed to restricted to using our pretty `/start` message. Decouples from `/start` more but obv still coupled with it slightly. Allows for simpler per-repo customization as you do not have to consider the `/start` setup also.

This plugin, really coupled together. The config will become big and messy probably and it adds a whole new branch of functionality to this worker.

here is an [example](https://www.github.com/safe-global/safe-smart-account/pull/789#issuecomment-2214809563)

title: Agentic exploration
body:
I’d like to propose enhancing the /ask plugin with agent-like capabilities, allowing the LLM to explore the repository, organization, or external resources as needed to answer a question more effectively.

For example, currently the LLM only has access to documents explicitly attached in the triggering comment. However, relevant information often exists elsewhere (such as in related issues/PRs, README, code files) that the LLM cannot currently access.

By enabling the LLM to explore more freely, we could greatly improve the quality and context-awareness of its responses.

The LLM agent could:
-	Access repo files: Fetch any file in the repo (e.g. source code, README, config files) to gain context.
-	Follow cross-references: Detect and fetch linked issues or PRs (e.g. `in #100 this was already implemented`) and retrieve their body or summarized comments.
-	Leverage external resources: Fetch linked documents or URLs from comments to extract additional context.
-	Explore related content: Automatically detect and pull in other relevant comments in the same issue that contain documents or links.

Use cases
-	When answering a question about a plugin, the LLM could fetch the README or main code file to better understand its purpose.
-	If someone references another issue (see #123), the LLM could fetch its description or comments to provide context.
-	If earlier comments contain documents or links, the LLM could use them even if they weren’t in the triggering comment.

Benefits
-	More complete and contextual answers
-	Reduced need for users to repeat or restate context
-	Smarter, more autonomous behavior aligned with how developers actually communicate

title: Feb 2025 Improvements
body:
### Summary

I attempted to use the `/ask` command to search for a statement referenced by @0x4007. However, the response lacked meaningful context or relevant embeddings. [^05^] Upon investigating the [action run](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-ask/actions/runs/13342393616/job/37268686368), I noticed potential issues with how similar issues and comments are retrieved, ranked, and formatted.

I spent around 30mins debugging and scanning over the code. I've also used AI to help structure and keep this as succinct as possible.

---

### Observations on Context Window

#### Current Context Retrieval Process:
- Finds the first 10 "similar comments" and 10 "similar issues" based on user input.
- Fetches the full issue for each of the 10 issues (and for each of the 10 comments too maybe)
- Uses a `rerank` function to combine and then separate issues and comments.
- Builds the `chatHistory`, then performs a second `rerank`.

#### Example Query:

`what did ox4007 recently say about corporate leadership have quarterly reviews with UbiquityOS, summarize that chain of events for me`

(Even with a minor typo, the query is clear and specific.)

However, the retrieved results were largely irrelevant.

---

### Irrelevant or Mismatched Context

1. **Issues & PRs Retrieved**
   - The first linked issue was about Alex's lack of communication and a payment dispute: [Issue #148](https://github.com/ubiquity/research/issues/148).
   - This was **not relevant** to the query, nor was it similar to [Issue #82](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pricing/issues/82). [^01^]
   - Other retrieved issues included:
     - [Credit System](https://github.com/ubiquity/.github/issues/110)
     - [Autonomous Coding Agent](https://github.com/ubiquity/.github/issues/105)
     - [Virtual Card Provider](https://github.com/ubiquity/card-issuance/issues/39)
     - [Payouts V2](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/174)
     - [Integrate Reloadly](https://github.com/ubiquity/card-issuance/issues/34)
     - [Card Issuance](https://github.com/ubiquity/card-issuance/issues/25)
     - [Tweaking Qualitative for Text-Conversation-Rewards](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/issues/97) (60+ comments)
     - [Reimplement Tracking Code](https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/issues/74)
     - My own PR: [`fix: close only assignee PR`](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/10)
     - [Fix Database Schema](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-vector-embeddings/issues/8)

   - Many of these are unrelated to the query and suggest **inefficient embedding matching or ranking.**

---

### Formatting Issues in Context Window

- **Duplicate Diff Snippets in Review Comments**
  - The same diffs are repeated for every review comment.
  - This redundancy might mislead the model into over-weighting certain sections as highly important. [^04^]
  
  **Potential Fix:** Group all comments from a review thread under a **single snapshot** of the relevant diff.

  **Example Screenshot of Issue:**
  ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/180a148f-57e0-41fb-8c5f-71c118e9ee96)

---

### Suggested Fixes & Next Steps

#### 1. **Refining the RAG Stack**
   - Remove reranking temporarily and test the base pipeline:  
     ```
     query → query embedding → DB function "find_similar_content" → analyze results
     ```
   - Evaluate whether the core retrieval logic is working before layering complexity.

#### 2. [^03^] [^02^] **Testing the `/ask` Command with Focused Evals**
   - While some evals are in place, the `/ask` command should be continually stress-tested in real scenarios.
   - Consider breaking down evaluations into smaller, isolated parts.

---

### Long-Term Concerns

1. **Scalability of Embeddings DB**
   - If embeddings continue to be added with every comment, the DB will grow noisier.
   - This could degrade retrieval quality over time.

2. [^03^] [^02^] **Fetching vs. Ranking Optimization**
   - If the issue is on the fetching side, optimizations could be simpler.
   - If it's fundamentally an embedding quality issue, the retrieval model might need adjustments.

3. **Adoption by Partners**
   - If accuracy declines, external partners may be less inclined to adopt using our chatbot.
   - I don't see a world where a partner will make effective use of our chatbot within their repos but fetching from our org history (the embeddings) so whatever we do for us needs to be pipelined in order for partner adoption of this feature to really flourish.

---

### Conclusion

The `/ask` command currently exhibits:
- **Inaccurate retrieval of relevant context.**
- **Redundant formatting issues affecting LLM interpretation.**
- **Potential long-term risks due to an expanding, noisy embeddings DB.**

Addressing these concerns via targeted debugging and structured evaluations should improve the accuracy and usability of this feature.

---

title: Code base Search
body:
The model can currently parse code files shared via links. However, this functionality should be improved to allow searching through the entire codebase repository where the bot operates. Similar solutions, like Copilot, chunk code into units, convert them into graphs, and use these for retrieval.

## Proposed Solution: AST-Based System for Codebase Queries

1. **Automatic Analysis**: The plugin would analyze the entire codebase, converting it into Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs).

2. **Chunking and Storage**: These ASTs would be segmented into meaningful units, such as functions, classes, and methods, and stored in tables with associated metadata, semantic descriptions, and vector embeddings in Supabase. These would be stored in three tables (AST_Nodes, Code_Chunks, Chunk_Relationships)

3. **Query Processing**: When a user submits a query, it would be converted into an embedding and used to search for similar code chunks. The system would retrieve relevant chunks, their relationships, and semantic descriptions from the database to effectively answer queries.

### repo/org/global Context Matching

I think we should optimize our logic. Tasks that may look similar but posted in two different repositories may in reality be quite different. Normally I would prefer to matchmake against those who completed similar tasks within the same repository, but we can "fallback" to org context (try to matchmake against any repository's task in the org) and then a final "fallback" to global context.

0% adjustment: Same repository matching percentage 
-25% adjustment: Same organization
-50%: Global

same repo = 100% match
same org, different repo = 75% match
different org = 50% match
```

Just an idea but open to discussing to make this more accurate and simple to implement.

Another idea to always try and match somebody is to check how much of the codebase was authored by whom. If nobody hits a relevance of greater than 25% we can fallback to assigning whoever wrote most of the code in the repository. Surely we can find the stats somewhere.

Because we want the system to always be assigning the right contributor at the right time in the future, we should consider the output of the `/start` command as well, with all its checks. title: Codebase semantic search
body:
For on boarding new developers, or just to synchronize existing developers, we should be generating embeddings of our code base. We can do per file or on the function level, depending on which has better performance.

I asked GPT for the best sorting method on the [embedding leaderboard](https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard). 

Later it clarified that we should be sorting by "retrieval with instructions" for best results. 

[FollowIR-7B](https://huggingface.co/jhu-clsp/FollowIR-7B) is the highest ranked. 

We should be doing this in two steps:
1. Primarily, we should be generating embeddings of the new files when pull requests are merged.
2. We should have a tool that we can run manually (manual dispatch on GitHub actions ok) to generate all the embeddings. This would be expected to be used if there were pushes directly to the default branch and were not added via pull request

### additional context

> For this use case (codebase question-answering), your focus should be on retrieval tasks. Based on the criteria provided, here’s how I would prioritize the metrics:

> 1. **Retrieval Average (15 datasets)**: This should be your highest priority. The better the retrieval capability of the model, the more relevant code chunks it will retrieve when you ask a question about the codebase.

> 2. **Embedding Dimensions**: A higher embedding dimension may provide more nuanced representations of code and questions, improving retrieval accuracy. However, this needs to be balanced with memory usage and model size.

> 3. **Model Size (Million Parameters)**: Larger models tend to perform better in generating high-quality embeddings, but at the cost of memory and speed. Consider how much memory and computational power you can afford.

> 4. **Max Tokens**: A higher max token limit is useful for code because some functions or files can be quite large. You'll want a model that can handle bigger chunks of code.

> 5. **Classification Average (12 datasets)**: Code-related tasks sometimes involve classification (e.g., determining the type of question or identifying sections of code). A higher classification score can help in such scenarios.

> 6. **STS Average (10 datasets)**: Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) is also important as it measures how well the embeddings capture semantic meaning, which is useful for understanding the context and retrieving the right code section.

> ### Sorting Criteria:
> Sort by **Retrieval Average** first, then consider **Max Tokens** and **Embedding Dimensions** for practical handling of code and performance optimization.

> The other metrics like **Classification**, **Clustering**, and **Reranking** are less critical for your specific use case, but they can help refine the quality if you have a secondary need for such tasks.

title: Centralizing Embeddings Access
body:
This plugin currently utilizes the same organization embeddings as `/ask`, `text-vector-`, etc., specifically for the `issues` and `issues_comments` tables. However, it also maintains its own tables for `chats`, `users`, and `session`. 

At present, the plugin operates with a **single DB instance** containing everything.

## Problem
We need to determine the best approach for managing embeddings access while maintaining scalability and avoiding redundancy not only for this plugin but for any that need it now or in the future.

## Potential Approaches

1. **Support Two DB Instances**  
   - One for embeddings access  
   - One for everything else  

2. **Spin Up a New DB Instance**  
   - Maintain synchronization between DBs  

3. **Create a Centralized Embeddings Plugin**  
   - A single service handles all embeddings access  

## Analysis

### Option 1: Two DB Instances  
❌ Messy and would need to be applied to other plugins in similar situations.  

### Option 2: Separate Instance with Syncing  
❌ Time-consuming, suboptimal, and adds maintenance overhead.  

### Option 3: Centralized Embeddings Plugin  
✅ Most scalable for future features.  
✅ Avoids duplication across plugins.  

### How Option 3 Works
- Right now how it works is that before any RAG operation, a user query is embedded, sent to the DB, and relevant content is retrieved. Each plugin handles this internally despite the only difference being the query and the chosen DB function for the given task. Something we could API through a plugin no problem.
- The plugin accepts a **string** and a **method** (e.g., `plugin("<task spec>", "similar-issues")`).
- The plugin returns relevant content, maintaining compatibility with existing workflows.

## Benefits of a Centralized Embeddings Plugin
- 📌 **Consolidates Embeddings Logic** – Simplifies codebase for contributors.  
- 🔧 **Removes Config Complexity** – No need for multiple DB connections.  
- 🚀 **Aligns with DAO Goals** – Encourages partners to utilize our infrastructure efficiently.  

## Next Steps
- Align on feasibility and implementation strategy.  
- Define the API interface for centralized embeddings access.  
- Plan migration for existing plugins relying on embeddings (starting with this one)

title: Improve `/ask` Command for Workrooms
body:
### Problem
The `/ask` command is currently used within newly created workrooms, which are intended to help contributors with their tasks. However, for knowledgeable users to assist, they must manually join and be present when contributors arrive, making the process inefficient.

### Proposed Solution
To make the `/ask` command more effective in workrooms, I propose the following improvements:

1. **Detect Chat Context**  
   - Identify the type of chat where the `/ask` command is used.
   - If it is a `workroom`, adjust behavior accordingly.

2. **Context-Aware Assistance**  
   - Instead of relying solely on the user's query to fetch content from the database (which may be unrelated), retrieve the current task context using the URL in the chat description similar to `/command-ask@V1&@V2` 
   - We can even pull the active PR details into context which would be a tremendous improvement in terms of being able to help.

3. **Guidance for New Contributors**  
   When a contributor joins a `workroom`, provide one of the following messages:
   - A private message: _"Use `/ask` to get help with this task."_
   - A public message: _"Use `/ask` to discuss this task with UbiquityOS."_

### Why?
Making the model's context more acutely-aware of the whole task will significantly improve the quality of assistance provided, ensuring that responses are directly relevant to the task and likely to be of more value.

### Handling Embeddings and Queries
If embeddings are current and functional, we could:
- Modify the user’s query before embedding, injecting references to the task at hand.
- Encourage users to include the task name/URL when asking questions.
- Filter on the DB side based on owner/repository which we can pull from the workroom title

title: Enhance Kernel with Generalized Request Handling & Secure External API
body:
#### **Summary**  
Expand the kernel's ingress beyond GitHub webhooks by introducing a secure public API endpoint. This will allow external services to trigger GitHub Actions workflows, effectively turning Actions into a general-purpose backend.  

#### **Key Features**  
- **Public API Endpoint**:  
  - Accepts external requests to execute plugins via the kernel.  
  - Supports dynamic execution of actions, enabling broader integrations.  

- **Authentication & Security**:  
  - Requests must include:  
    - `installation ID` (this allows us to target the correct org)  
    - `repository ID` (optionally, to load a specific repo config)  
  - Partners must provide an **encrypted password** stored in their config.  
    - Uses **X25519 encryption** (same system as EVM private key storage).  
    - Clients pass a password in the request header, which the kernel decrypts.  
  - Rate-limiting to prevent abuse.  

- **Execution Flow**:  
  1. Kernel receives an authenticated request with at least `installation ID` and `password`.  
  2. It decrypts the password and verifies the request.  
  3. Executes the specified plugin and returns the response.  

- **Webhook Replies**:  
  - Requests can include a `response URL` header.  
  - The kernel posts the result from the action plugin to this URL upon completion.

https://github.com/ferrislucas/iterm-mcp/blob/961882be693b82e258408f24ca1f40ee0a96e033/src/index.ts#L25-L72

To be honest it isn't clear to me if we must make all of our plugins into MCP servers, or if we just make our kernel into an MCP server.

title: Decrypt sensitive config parameters
body:
Right now there are 2 ways to hide sensitive bot's config parameters:
1. Make a config repository private (organization collaborators can still see the values though)
2. Fork plugin, self host and set sensitive parameters in env variables (bad UX for partners)

Sensitive config parameters could be encrypted via our own `x25519_PUBLIC_KEY` (the same one we use for encrypting partners' private keys) and the kernel could then decrypt them.

So as a part of this issue the kernel should be able to decrypt config parameters on initial config parsing. 

The expected flow for parsing a single config param:
1. Try to decrypt the parameter. 
2. If it is decrypted then use the decrypted parameter.
3. If there's a decryption error then assume the parameter is not encrypted and use a raw value.

Notice that there is a difference between decrypting: 
1. Unencrypted param
2. Encrypted param with another PK

I hope https://doc.libsodium.org/ distinguishes those 2 errors because in the 2nd case it will be a very subtle bug and the kernel should ideally throw an error like `The config parameter encryption is invalid` so that partner knew he did something wrong on encrypting a param.

P.S. Handy tool: https://keygen.ubq.fi/

title: Infinite loop using wildcard event
body:
Recently we suffered from infinite loops in the kernel combined with actions. After investigating, it seems that the combination of the wildcard event (`'*'`) with an Action was the cause. What happens is the following:
- the kernel receives a webhook event, say a `push` event
- the kernel dispatches that event to plugins located within `'*'`
- the action starts, say `user-activity-watcher`
- this summons the Github webhook that sends a `workflow_started` event to the kernel
- kernel dispatches that event to `'*'`
- action starts again

and so on, creating the loop. It doesn't happen with Workers because they don't trigger any event within Github when they are run.

I think this highlights the dangers of subscribing Actions to that wildcard. Maybe we should consider removing it and changing the way we configure plugins. My idea was to have a `allow | forbid` list where we can configure which events to react to, or which events to ignore, per plugin in the configuration file. Now that we are working on the [manifest feature](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-kernel/issues/58), we could even allow plugin creators to set some defaults there, that we can eventually override within the configuration.

However despite these changes we would not be safe from infinite loops (for example, a plugin posting a comment when the event comment posting is triggered). We should think of a way to limit runs if that happens, to avoid bursting through cloudflare limits and github api.

title: Deadlines Incentive
body:
After a few calls with prospective pilot partners, it’s clear that teams care about **accurate time estimates** and **incentivizing deadlines**. This command should make deadlines more useful while rewarding contributors fairly.  

---

## **Objective**  
Build the **command-deadline plugin** to:  
1. **Encourage accurate time estimates** by tracking task durations.  
2. **Reward early completion** while ensuring deadlines matter.  

---

## **How It Works**  

### **Setting a Deadline**  
- Use `/deadline [date]` to set a deadline on a GitHub issue.  
- The deadline is tied to UTC by default but can be configured.  
- If a GitHub Project View is linked, the GitHub issue should sync there on the timeline view (if configured).  

### **Rewarding Early Completion**  
By default, finishing a task **on time** earns **100% of the task value**. If completed **faster**, the contributor gets a **speed bonus**. If **late**, they either receive **a reduced payout or are disqualified** (configurable).  

---

## **Deadline Reward Ratio Configuration**  

Instead of always giving **double the task value** for instant completion, we introduce a **configurable coefficient**:  

- **`deadlineRewardRatio`** → Controls how much of the task value is used for speed bonuses.  
- Default is `0.25`, meaning a max bonus of **25% extra** for instant completion.  
- If set to `1.0`, instant completion can **double** the reward.  

For example, on a **$1600** task with `deadlineRewardRatio = 0.25`:  
- **Instant completion** → `$1600 + $400 bonus = $2000`  
- **Halfway to deadline** → `$1600 + $200 bonus = $1800`  
- **On deadline** → `$1600` (no bonus, no penalty)  
- **Past deadline** → Payout gradually decreases unless disqualification is enabled.  

---

## **Final Reward Formula**  

```text
reward = baseTaskValue * max(0, 1 + (deadlineRewardRatio * (1 - (actualCompletionTime / assignedDeadline))) - ((1 - disqualificationEnabled) * (actualCompletionTime / assignedDeadline)))
```

### **How It Works**  
- **If completed early**, the reward increases up to `1 + deadlineRewardRatio` times the base task value.  
- **If completed exactly on time**, the reward is **1× task value**.  
- **If late**:
  - If **disqualification is enabled**, the reward drops to **0** at `assignedDeadline`.  
  - If **disqualification is disabled**, the reward **gradually decreases** until **0 at `2 * assignedDeadline`**.  

---

## **Disqualification (Optional)**  
If enabled, contributors **must** complete the task before the deadline or they receive **nothing**. This can be toggled per project.  

---

### **Mock YAML Configuration File**
Here’s a **sample `config.yml`** with all possible settings and their **default values**:

```yaml
commandDeadline:
  timezone: "UTC"  # Default timezone for deadlines (UTC, PST, etc.)
  deadlineRewardRatio: 0.25  # Max speed bonus (0.25 = 25% extra, 1.0 = 100% extra)
  disqualificationEnabled: true  # Whether missing the deadline results in a 0 reward
  projectView: null  # Link to GitHub Project View if deadlines should sync there
```

### **Configurable Behavior**
- If `deadlineRewardRatio = 0.5`, contributors **can earn up to 50% extra** for early completion.  
- If `disqualificationEnabled = false`, contributors **still get some payout even if late**, but it gradually declines.  
- If `projectView` is set, deadlines will be **synced to the linked GitHub Project View**.  

---

### **Final Summary**
- `/deadline [date]` sets a deadline.  
- **Early = Bonus** (configurable via `deadlineRewardRatio`).  
- **On time = Full payout**.  
- **Late = Configurable penalty (default: disqualification, or gradual payout reduction if disabled)**.  
- **Deadlines can sync to GitHub Project Views** if linked.  

This setup keeps the system **flexible, fair, and easy to configure**.

title: New Task Or Edit Pull Arbiter
body:
### Overview

- During pull requests, we need to have a bias of always moving forward. 
- We always need to make an active decision on whether to include requested changes in the current pull or if we should break them off into new tasks. 
- We should use an LLM to help us decide what to do. 

### Ideal Outcome

We seamlessly can review pulls and then the OS can intelligently create a new issue batching the requested changes and link back. Ideal if it can batch similar tasks aiming for between 1 hour and 1 day within the same GitHub issue (I think this is possible with my experience working with Claude 3.5 Sonnet.)

### Implementation

The way that this can work is if we leave the review state as "commented" and leave comments that seem like we want changes to be done. These will need to be understood by the OS. 

If we really think the changes are critical to be done in the current pull, then we must be sure to "request changes." 

### Remarks

I am concerned that it might be too quick to fire off new issues, so ideally we have it understand that there is a possibly already created "post pull request review" task, and to continue batching everything from the review in that task (we could standardize the naming scheme of the generated issue.) 

We may possibly need to check for pull request closed and merged to process the full conversation and fire off new tasks.  This will allow us room to determine the necessity of such suggestions.

Developer Referrals
body:
In order to increase the size of our developer community, we should pay who refer developers who contribute. Let's call them DevRels.

The vision is to generate a new permit for the DevRel upon task completion. 
- It is unclear to me exactly how to do default pricing (flat fee, percentage) 
- It can be easy to game and squeeze out extra rewards with a self referral unless the DevRel's cut is zero sum from the developer. If it is zero sum, then a percentage would be safest i.e. 5% or 10%. What is the highest percentage we can go before developers get annoyed? Perhaps we can also set a max cap, like 50 USD per reward in addition to the percentage. For example, if a developer receives a 1000 USD reward, perhaps the DevRel cap can be max 50 USD. 
- I fear the rewards may not be very competitive. We can consider high (non zero sum) rewards in the short term to kick things off, then switch it to zero sum mode later.
- We should also consider a reward for every developer referred (this may be implemented as a separate tool though, because it seems incompatible with the percentage or zero sum system)

### Configuration Requirements

- For version one, lets go only with percentages support. Make sure that the percentage is configurable. 
   - This will keep things simple in case the DevRel earns a tiny reward for leaving a small comment etc.
- Make sure that we can toggle zero sum mode (subtract from developer reward to pay the DevRel.) 

### Implementation Overview

We can do this in a couple of parts:
1. the new referral logs in with GitHub at `work.ubq.fi?ref=[github user id of DevRel]` 
2. we associate in a KV store the key being the DevRel GitHub ID and the value being an array of DevRel values. 
```typescript
type GitHubId = number;
type KV = { [key: GitHubId]: GitHubId[] };
```

This feels a little parasitic if a developer accidentally clicks a DevRel's link at some point in the future, especially if they start losing some of their rewards. I think we need some type of system to "undo" a referral. This doesn't feel like the right solution but I'm unsure what is. 

### Sybils
We can protect against sybils based on the age of a GitHub profile as well as a minimum XP requirement. For example, if the developer XP is low then the rewards are zero sum?

title: Allow Users to Select and Configure Specific Plugin Branches
body:
Currently, the plugin installer GUI assumes users always want to configure and install the version of a plugin found on a single, predefined branch (initially hardcoded to `development`, later updated to the repository's default branch). However, plugins often have different versions, features, or configuration schemas across various branches (e.g., `main`, `development`, feature branches, release tags).

Users need the ability to explicitly select the desired branch for a plugin they are configuring, and the system must ensure that the correct manifest is used for rendering the UI and the correct identifier (Action reference or URL) is saved in the configuration file.

**Desired Behavior / Acceptance Criteria:**

1.  The configuration editor should display a dropdown allowing users to select from the available branches of the plugin's source repository.
2.  When editing an existing plugin configuration, the dropdown should pre-select the branch specified in the saved configuration identifier (`owner/repo@branch` or parsed from URL).
3.  When editing an existing plugin configuration, the editor UI should initially render based on the manifest fetched from the *configured* branch.
4.  When the user selects a different branch from the dropdown, the editor UI should dynamically update by fetching and rendering the manifest from the newly selected branch.
5.  When saving the configuration, the `plugin` identifier stored in the `uses` array must accurately reflect the user's selected branch:
    *   For Action-based plugins: `owner/repo@selectedBranch`
    *   For URL-based plugins: The correctly transformed URL corresponding to the `selectedBranch` (e.g., `https://...-selected-branch-suffix.domain.com`).
6.  UI elements should be consistent with the rest of the application.
7.  Informational/success toast notifications should auto-dismiss.

## Main issues

We will have problems saving different branches because it is technically correct to have two similar plugins pointing to two different branches. Similarly the plugin would not know we want to change the target branch but will instead stack plugins from different branches together.

title: premade configs that are hands-off for partners
body:
## Premade Configurations vs. Default Plugin Manifests

We aim to streamline the experience for pilot partners by providing **premade configurations**. This approach reduces the need for partners to manually configure plugins. In addition, we provide two alternative ways to modify configurations:

1. Utilize [this feature request](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugins-wishlist/issues/65).
2. Contact customer support for manual adjustments.

### Default Plugin Behavior

1. When a plugin uses `defaults` that are **not** sourced from a **premade config**, it retrieves its configuration from the plugin's `manifest.json` in its respective repository.
2. These defaults originate from `pluginInputs.ts` and are used across multiple infrastructure components, including:
   - This UI
   - Natural language configuration edits
   - Plugin schema and input validation (kernel-side)
   - Other relevant subsystems

#### Opinionated Defaults

There is a general concern about **opinionated defaults**. Instead of enforcing such defaults, we should **only share premade configs with partners**, eliminating the need for them to define their own configurations.

Reference: [Discussion on opinionated defaults](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/151#discussion_r1991092437)

### Configuration Modes

Currently, there are three configuration modes:

- **Minimal**
- **Full Defaults**
- **Custom**

These modes, up to this point, have not been enforced to be unopinionated. Some configurations are highly opinionated and may not align with the principle of **non-opinionated defaults**.

---

## Proposed Solutions

### 1. Establish a Collection of Premade Configurations
- Define a structured set of **premade configs**.
- Ensure each premade config abstracts its functionality at a high level.
- Reduce the cognitive load on partners.

### 2. YAML-Based Template Structure
To further simplify configuration management, I suggest we use a **YAML template** with the following structure:

```yaml
metadata:
  name: "UbiquityOS Standard Config"
  description: "The fully-enabled and battle-tested configuration which we use across all organizations at Ubiquity."
  version: "1.0"

plugins: ...
```

This template includes:
- **Metadata**: Describes the premade configuration.
- **Plugins**: Lists installed plugins with relevant settings.

This abstraction ensures partners **"don’t have to think about it."**

---

## Handling Plugin Expansion

### Default Non-Expanded Behavior
@gentlementlegen [suggests](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/issues/40#issuecomment-2670919061) that plugins should be installed in a **non-expanded state**. This means:

- **Infra fetches only the non-opinionated defaults** when retrieving the plugin’s manifest.
- **If plugin details are expanded**, infra should fetch its specific config **before** relying on the manifest.

### Supporting Only Premade Configs
If we only allow **premade configs** and restrict editing to **already installed plugins**, then:

- Each `premade` configuration will be expanded by default.
- This ensures we avoid relying on **non-opinionated defaults**, which may not align with intended user experiences.

---

## Conclusion

- **Premade configurations** should be the standard approach.
- A **YAML-based template** simplifies configuration abstraction.
- **Non-expanded installations** should default to non-opinionated configurations.
- **Expanded plugin configurations** should fetch predefined configurations before falling back to defaults.

By enforcing these principles, we create a **streamlined, user-friendly**, and **low-maintenance** approach to plugin configuration management.

title: Multiple Org Install
body:
Right now it's only possible to update one org config at a time so we should consider adding logic for pushing to multiple orgs which would be a great QOL improvement for those with multiple installs to tend to (like we do)

1. Present the choice within the `orgSelector` to enable multi-select
2. Present the choice just before push via a notification something like `Are you sure you want to push to Ubiquity? "continue" | "push to more" | "cancel"`

Without this feature, we'd need to run the UI flow 4 times to update one plugin which is not ideal.

- We might need to have the user confirm which org config to use to fill in existing values. We could do this simply by using `selectedOrgs[0]` or making it a specific interaction to choose.
- If selecting a template like `minimal` or `full_defaults`, I'd assume we'd overwrite their entire existing config in all orgs if there is one, as we could end up with duplicate plugins otherwise
- repo and file creation for all selected orgs should be covered too



Relates to https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugins-wishlist/issues/57

title: Octokit helper methods
body:
We are using two GraphQL queries for fetching linked issues and fetching linked PRs so the code gets duplicated in each plugin that needs it. 

I think this is helpful for a couple of reasons:
- No duplication of code
- Less bugs because currently each repo have its own implementation (daemon-pull-reviewer's implementation was typed wrongly causing a bug)
- New contributors can use these helper methods without having to worry about implementation

Octokit supports plugins which essentially add methods to the Octokit object. 
Example usage:
```js
octokit.helpers.getLinkedIssues({
  owner,
  repo,
  prNumber
})
octokit.helpers.getLinkedPullRequests({
  owner,
  repo,
  issueNumber
})
```

This is so a dev can create handlers for multiple webhook events and the SDK process them all as a single fn for any given event.

`Proxy` logic has been simplified via the new `CallbackBuilder` and the SDK should export it. (This task may need transferred into the SDK if it's no longer exported from this repo)

body:

- Top performers (via USD earned, tasks completed, reviews performed, etc)

Each should have it's own view separate from the rest. The UI currently has everything squashed together via `legends` and stuffed into the chart bar details etc.

title: Monetizing analytics
body:
I put forth this little project after a comment regarding a business priority which is monetizing our eco-system and it was agreed that analytics is something that falls into something that we can monetize.

# Goals
1. Create a service like a GitHub app subscription (maybe) and have it encapsulate this repo and it's offering.
2. Implement various forms of analysis that provide value to the app user (an org).
3. Provide enough value through our analysis that would justify it being a separate 'add-on' (this can also work for orgs which do not have UbiquityOS installed - they'd be limited to retroactive fetching tho).

# Decisions to be made
1. If targeting all contributors of the org and not just members then `charge per seat` can't be a valid choice i'd imagine.
2. Should it be strictly for orgs which have a UbiquityOS install?
3. What high value areas or niches can we fill with our analytics beyond what's naturally expected?
4. `Github Storage` needs to be assigned to a team member and worked on, as @0x4007 you keep repeating it and it's got `???` assigned to it in the org readme. I already started working on it, if you want to me to continue on my implementation and see it through to the SDK let me know.

- [ ] UI: Replace static data with data source chosen above (likely repo JSON)

The above will get it to an "active" state that allows it to be used, from there we'd quickly iterate on expanding and improving the fetching, analysis and UI design.

Notes:

- [`/plugin-or-cli`](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/dao-analytics/tree/main/plugin-or-cli) - is responsible for data collection and is probs 80% ready. It's built for retroactive right now but only tested as a script not as a plugin (it'll need to be an action as it's a long execution time).
